Disclosure to Promote the Right To Information 

Whereas the Parliament of India has set out to provide a practical regime of right to 
information for citizens to secure access to information under the control of public authorities, 
in order to promote transparency and accountability in the working of every public authority, 
and whereas the attached publication of the Bureau of Indian Standards is of particular interest 
to the public, particularly disadvantaged communities and those engaged in the pursuit of 
education and knowledge, the attached public safety standard is made available to promote the 
timely dissemination of this information in an accurate manner to the public.

IS : 10212 ( Part 1 ) - 1986 

Indian Standard 

GENERAL REQUIREMENTS OF 
PACKAGES FOR EXPLOSIVES 

PART 1 COMMERCIAL HIGH EXPLOSIVES 

(First Revision) 



0. FOREWORD 

0.1 This Indian Standard ( Part 1 ) ( First Revision ) was adopted by 
the Indian Standards Institution on 20 June 1986, after the draft finalized 
by the Packaging of Chemicals Sectional Committee had been approved 
by the Marine, Cargo Movement and Packaging Division Council. 

0.2 This standard ( Part 1 ) first published in 1982 has been revised to 
make certain modifications keeping in view the requirements of the 
explosive manufacturers. This revision also provides flexibility with 
regard to the style of the package subject to the prior approval of the 
Chief Controller of Explosives. 

0.3 Increased production and use of comineicial explosives has resulted 
in the introduction of variety of their packages. The inner and outer 
packages provide necessary protection to the explosive, especially during 
their transit. The Explosives Rules, 1983 framed under the Explosives Act, 
1884 provides the detailed stipulations for the packaging and storage of 
explosives. However, the strength and water resistance requirements for 
the outer packages or transport packages have been covered by this 
standard. 

0.4 Explosives are classified according to IS : 1446-1959* into three types 
as follows: 

Type 1 (a) Explosives with a mass explosion risk; 

Type 1 (b) Explosives which do not explode enmasse but which 
have a limited explosion or fire hazard or both; and 

Type 1 (c) Explosives having mass fire hazards. 



* Classification of dangerous goods* 



18 i 10212 ( Pmrt 1 ) - 1986 

0.5 This standard ( Part 1 ) covers only the packages for explosives of 
Type 1 (a), such as gun powder, nitroglycerine based gelatine explosives, 
slurry or water-gel explosives, detonating fuse, detonators, etc, subsequent 
parts will cover packages for Types 1 (b) and 1 (c) explosives. 



1. SCOPE 

1.1 This standard ( Part 1 ) prescribes the requirements of packages for 
high explosives meant for commercial use. 

2. TERMINOLOGY 

2.1 For the purpose of this standard, definitions as given in IS : 1446- 
1959* and IS : 10081-lC81t shall apply. 

3. PACKAGE 

3.1 Inner Package — The inner packaging of the contents shall be in 
accordance with the requirements laid down by the Chief Controller of 
Explosives. 

3*2 Outer Package — The outer packaging for the commercial high 
explosives shall meet the requirements prescribed in 3.4. The specifica- 
tion for corrugated fibreboard packages and wooden packages as outer 
package to fulfil these requirements are given in Appendix A. 

3.3 Maximum Permiasible Mass — No package shall contain a mass 
exceeding 25 kg. This limit conforms to the provision of the statutory 
requirements. 

3.4 Performance Requirement — The outer package shall withstand 
the tests and conditions thereof as given in Table 1. These are type 
tests. 

4. MARKING

41.1 The package may also be marked with Standard Mark. 



4.1.2 The use of the Standard Mark is governed by the provisions of Bureau of 
Indian Standards Act, 1986 and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. 
The details of conditions under which the licence for the use of Standard Mark 
may be granted to manufacturers or producers may be obtained from the Bureau 
of Indian Standards. 



5. SAMPLING, CONDITIONING AND TESTING OF CPB 
PACKAGES 

5.1 The packages shall be sampled and tested within 20 days of their 
receipt by the purchaser. From each consignment of 10 000 packages or 
part thereof, adequate number of packages shall be selected for testing 
according to 5.3. 

5.1.1 If the packages are bundled, the number of bundles to be selected 
at random shall be equal to the number of packages required and from 
each bundle so selected one package shall be selected at random for 
testing. 

5.1.2 If the packages are not bundled, the packages shall be selected at 
random from the total consignment. 

SJt Conditioning — The sample of packages so selected shall be 
deemed to represent the whole consignment of packages and shall be 
conditioned testing by the method prescribed in 5 of IS : 1060 ( Part 1 )• 
I966». 

5.S Tearing 

5w3«l The types of tests, selection of packages for testing and method of 
testing shall be as given in Table 2. 

5.4 Aceeptaace and Reletting 

5.4.1 Acaptanct — The consignment of packages shall be deemed to 
comply with the test requirements of this specification, if after the 
specified number of packages from the test sample as given in Table 2 
have been tested as required in relevant clauses and all the packages pass 
the tests*

5.4*2 RiUsting —If only one package fails to pass one or more tests, 
retesting shall be done on double the number of packages given under 
col 2 of Table 2 for that particular test for which the package failed. If 
no further package fails in the reicst, the consignment shall be accepted 
as passing.
